newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast light crudes follow gasoline's lead.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast light crudes follow gasoline's lead.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices rose, following NYMEX crude as it climbed on talk a major refiner bought spot gasoline in the Gulf Coast market.
NYMEX December crude followed the lead of unleaded gasoline futures, which rose as much as 1.65 cents a gallon during Monday's session.
Crude settled a penny lower, but gained as much as 49 cents a barrel before settling at $24.85 a barrel.
Discounts for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude remained notionally unchanged at $2.30 a barrel off December WTI, while buyers speculated a deal occured near that level.
The ANS spot basis shifted from November to December Monday, with outright ANS prices $22.90/23.20 a barrel.
Ultramar Corp began unspecified run cuts at its Wilmington, Calif, refinery over the weekend. Cuts came after workers shut a coker and other units, an industry source said.
Wilmington crude held at $18.90/19 a barrel.
Kern River heavy crude also held, ranging $17.40 to 17.60 a barrel, with majors and a large independent refiner rumored to offer cargoes. --David Brinkerhoff, Los Angeles energy +1 213 380 2014
